clue.text: Scores talk about doctor's last case

indicators.note: the talk goes about, that is around, the other pieces

parts.note: an oration is a formal talk or speech

indicators.note: only the final letter of the abbreviation for doctor is kept

parts.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor
a chest is a large box or case

explanation.surface: Musical scores discuss what happened in the doctor's latest medical case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suits the doctor's surface as a patient, but it means a box; 'doctor's last' takes the final letter of the abbreviation DR, not of the word doctor's.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestrations are arrangements of music for orchestra, written out as scores.

clue.text: Frank is very involved with unit in education centre

parts.note: frank and open both mean candid

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters of these words are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A candid person is closely involved with a department at a teaching centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' rearranges the letters of IS VERY and UNIT, giving UNIVERSITY. The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open University is a British institution offering degrees by distance learning, a place of higher education.

clue.text: Chief put away person who has had one

parts.note: CH is an abbreviation for chief, as in Ch Supt
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A boss locks away someone who has had something, perhaps a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' here is slang for tricked or swindled: someone who has had one has fooled a victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is someone who has 'had' another person, slang for deceived them.

clue.text: Helped end a hunt organised in European continent

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the European continent pieces

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone helped finish off a fox hunt arranged somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' mixes up A HUNT, and 'in' places the result between the European and continent pieces. 'Helped end' reads as a verb phrase but is a noun: an end that was helped.
explanation.definitionFit: Assisted dying is a death brought about with help, so a helped end.

clue.text: Biggest supporter in ground hit bouncer close to exit

parts.note: to tap is to hit lightly
a roo, a kangaroo, bounces along

indicators.note: close means end here, so only the final letter of exit is taken

explanation.surface: The heaviest backer at a sports ground struck a doorman near the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' and 'bouncer' suggest a football stadium and a nightclub doorman; the ground is soil and the bouncer a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's main downward root is its biggest underground support, holding it in the soil.

clue.text: A very low increase in brief

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: A tiny pay rise is mentioned in a briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' is the verb, as a lawyer is briefed; 'very low' means very quiet in music.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to inform them, give them the facts.

clue.text: Paper working to limit Republican club

indicators.note: to limit is to bound on both sides, so the paper and working pieces surround the Republican letter

parts.note: I is the Independent, a British newspaper
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A newspaper is trying to restrict a Republican society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society to match the political surface, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, an iron is a type of club with a metal head.

clue.text: Tyneside became consumed by one broker

indicators.note: by means beside, so the consumed piece comes right next to the one piece

parts.note: NE, North East, is the region of England containing Tyneside
got means became, as in got angry
I is the Roman numeral for one
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Northeast England was swallowed up by a single stockbroker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broker' is a verb here, as in to broker a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To broker an agreement is to arrange it through discussion between parties.

clue.text: Obscure name in company entitled to hold line

indicators.note: the name letter goes inside the company piece

parts.note: a unit is a company, as of soldiers

indicators.note: the entitled piece holds the line letter within it

parts.note: eligible means entitled or qualified

explanation.surface: A little-known name in a firm qualifies to take a position on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective about the name; it is the definition, meaning hard to make out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure, impossible to understand, is incomprehensible.

clue.text: Badminton competition's opening by end of June

indicators.note: by means beside, so the opening comes right next to the final letter of June
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A badminton tournament starts at the end of June.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton is also the Badminton Horse Trials, a famous English equestrian three-day event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Badminton Horse Trials are a three-day equestrian competition, and each contest is an event.

clue.text: Stone work unit hiding old article stops here

parts.note: a pip is a fruit stone

indicators.note: the work unit hides the old letter within it

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A stonemason's work unit hides an antique, and the stopping happens here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' looks like a verb, but is the noun: the knobs that control an organ's ranks of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ has stops, the controls that bring sets of pipes into play, so it is where stops are found.

clue.text: Court nails suspect without hearing

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful, not sound, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A court convicts a suspect without giving them a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hearing' sounds legal but means outside the range of human hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultrasonic sound has a frequency too high for people to hear.

clue.text: Recurved bananas make quite an impact

indicators.note: something recurved is bent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bananas and nuts both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Curved bananas are quite striking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit to go with 'Recurved', but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish, which is to make a strong impression.

clue.text: Girls go after celebrated shades

indicators.note: the girls piece goes after the celebrated piece

parts.note: sung means celebrated, as a hero is sung in verse
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Girls chase a famous person's shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go after' looks like chasing, but only fixes the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades is informal for tinted spectacles worn against the glare.

clue.text: Embed motorway scheme within it

indicators.note: the motorway and scheme pieces go within the word it

parts.note: taken as written
M is used for a motorway, as in the M1
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: Build a road project into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' at the end is not a pronoun for the answer; its two letters wrap round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant something is to fix it firmly inside, as tissue or a device in the body.

clue.text: Evidence I've altered implicating King's Head music man

indicators.note: implicating means involving, so the king's head letter is folded into the evidence

parts.note: proof is evidence

indicators.note: altered means changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Evidence has been doctored to implicate the head of state in a musical scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges the letters of I've; 'implicating' puts the first letter of King's, signalled by 'Head', inside the evidence piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Prokofiev was a Russian composer, of Peter and the Wolf and Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Old coin found in early English school

indicators.note: the coin is found inside the abbreviation for early English

parts.note: EE stands for Early English, the medieval style of Gothic architecture
the ducat was an old gold coin of Europe

explanation.surface: An antique coin was discovered at an old English school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun but is the verb, to train or teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them.

clue.text: Sculptor's inside say scraping away

indicators.note: the sculptor is inside, that is placed within, the piece for say

parts.note: EG, for example, means say
the sculptor is Auguste Rodin, and 's means is

explanation.surface: A sculptor at work, scraping away at the stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sculptor's' as 'Sculptor is': the sculptor's name is inside the abbreviation for 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroding means wearing away gradually, as wind and water abrade rock.

clue.text: Stargazer's delay over current constellation

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is reversed in a down clue

parts.note: lag means delay
I is the symbol for electric current
Leo, the lion, is a constellation

explanation.surface: An astronomer's hold-up concerning the current constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' signals reading upwards, so the word for delay is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer who pioneered observing the heavens through a telescope.

clue.text: Response to derisory offer from bishop good in principle

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the good letter goes inside the principle

parts.note: an ideal is a principle

explanation.surface: A bishop's offer may be fine in principle, but the reply is scornful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts G inside IDEAL, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ironic exclamation 'So what!' greets something unimpressive, as a mean offer is.

clue.text: Say nothing ousting mapmakers in Bosnia plant

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so the say and nothing pieces replace the mapmakers in Bosnia

parts.note: OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's official mapping agency
EG, for example, means say
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about cartographers being expelled from a Bosnian plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say nothing' looks like one idea, keep quiet, but gives EG and O, which take the place of OS in BOSNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The begonia is a flowering garden and houseplant.

clue.text: Keen student's wife ensconced in boozer

indicators.note: ensconced means settled in, so the wife letter sits inside the boozer

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard, a boozer

explanation.surface: An eager student's wife is settled in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' is British slang for a pub, but here means a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is British slang for someone who studies hard.

clue.text: Identify comic penning verse, in declaring his allegiance?

parts.note: to flag something is to identify or mark it

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the comic piece encloses the verse and in pieces

parts.note: a wag is a comic, a joker
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spot a comedian writing a verse in which he declares his loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word: with V it goes inside WAG to make WAVING.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag-waving is a patriotic display, a showy demonstration of loyalty to one's country.

clue.text: Nice night following one husky driver?

indicators.note: the Nice night piece follows the one piece

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
nuit is French for night, and Nice is a French city

explanation.surface: A pleasant evening after one hoarse-voiced chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the French city, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit people of the Arctic traditionally drive teams of husky dogs pulling sledges.

clue.text: Boss initially takes in south of France

indicators.note: the first letter goes in the French word for south

parts.note: sud is French for south

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: The boss first heads for the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of France' is not the Riviera but the French word for south.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a raised ornamental knob, as is a boss on a shield.

clue.text: 9 attempt to be heard by Irish town briefly

indicators.note: to be heard means spoken aloud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Athlone is a town in the middle of Ireland

explanation.surface: An event involves trying to be heard in a small Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points to the answer at 9 across, a competition, of which this is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon of swimming, cycling and running is a sporting event, as 9 across means.

clue.text: Gourmets quibble, eating banger

indicators.note: the outer words are eating, that is holding inside them, the answer

explanation.surface: Food lovers argue over eating a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' is British slang for a sausage, fitting the gourmets, but here is a firework that bangs.
explanation.definitionFit: A squib is a small firework that explodes with a bang.

clue.text: Consult old patient about earth recording

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in texts to mean consult a reference

indicators.note: the patient goes about, that is around, the earth

parts.note: a case is a patient in medical usage
a sett is a badger's earth, its burrow

explanation.surface: See an elderly patient concerning a land registry record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' is not soil or the planet but a badger's burrow; 'Consult' is the Latin instruction used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A videocassette is a tape cartridge holding a recording of film or television.
